body.statement:
Proposition 1 of Stoye2007ManyTreatments characterizes the many-treatment minimax-regret allocation correspondence and value as the argmin and minimum over \(q\in\Delta_K\) of
\[
 \max_{a\in\mathcal A}\left\{(1-q_a)U_{ax}-\sum_{c\neq a}q_cL_{cx}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: The decision maker chooses a treatment rule δ ∈ Δ. Nature chooses a potentially mixed strategy σ, that is, a distribution over states of the world. The decision maker's loss is R(δ,s) ≡ max_t {μ_t} − ∑_t δ_t μ_t. Then there exist convex sets D* and S* such that (δ*,σ*) is a Nash equilibrium if and only if (δ*,σ*) ∈ D* × S*; furthermore, D* is the set of minimax regret treatment rules. Thus, Nature always has a best response in the set {s_t}, where s_t places treatment t at its upper bound and every other treatment at its lower bound.
